audit_scope.description: Trust model analysis for Ethereum protocol specifications covering EVM opcodes, network protocols, and fork implementations. This batch focuses on state access opcodes (EXTCODEHASH), logging mechanisms (LOG opcodes), peer-to-peer networking (etha protocol), transaction processing (Shanghai fork), and security primitives (STATICCALL).

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitters via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External users and applications submit signed transactions through JSON-RPC endpoints. These entities are untrusted as they may submit malicious transactions, attempt DoS attacks via resource-intensive operations, or exploit vulnerabilities. All transactions must undergo validation (signature verification, nonce checks, balance checks, gas limits) before execution.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Ethereum Nodes (P2P Network)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P Network Protocol (DevP2P, etha subprotocol handshake)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Remote Ethereum nodes connecting via P2P protocols (including the etha subprotocol for historical data availability). Peers are untrusted as they may: (1) advertise false data availability via blockBitmask, (2) send invalid blocks or malformed messages, (3) attempt eclipse or DoS attacks, (4) provide incorrect historical data. All peer-provided data requires validation including handshake parameter verification (networkId, genesis hash, forkId) and block/transaction validation.

trusted_external_entities.name: Ethereum P2P Network Layer
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P Network Protocol (Block and Transaction Propagation)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The underlying network layer that propagates blocks, transactions, and protocol messages between nodes. This is untrusted as the network may be compromised or manipulated through: (1) eclipse attacks isolating nodes, (2) message injection or tampering, (3) timing attacks, (4) network partitioning. All network-received data must be cryptographically verified and validated before processing.

trusted_external_entities.name: Application Layer Requesting Historical Data
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Higher-level applications requesting historical blockchain data through RPC APIs. While these are local applications, they are untrusted as they may: (1) request excessive data causing DoS, (2) exploit rate limiting or resource exhaustion vulnerabilities, (3) attempt to extract sensitive information about node state. Requests must be rate-limited and resource-bounded.

trusted_external_entities.name: External Smart Contracts
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: EVM Execution Engine (CALL, DELEGATECALL, STATICCALL opcodes)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External smart contracts that may be invoked through inter-contract calls. These are untrusted as they may contain malicious code designed to: (1) exploit re-entrancy vulnerabilities, (2) manipulate state during callbacks, (3) consume excessive gas, (4) violate invariants of calling contracts. Protection mechanisms include STATICCALL for read-only operations, gas limits, and proper re-entrancy guards in calling contracts.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: All submitted transactions are validated for: (1) valid ECDSA signature matching sender address, (2) sufficient sender balance to cover gas and value transfer, (3) correct nonce matching account state, (4) gas limit within block gas limit bounds, (5) valid transaction format and encoding. Invalid transactions are rejected before entering the transaction pool or EVM execution.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: P2P Network Protocol (DevP2P, etha subprotocol handshake)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Peer handshake is validated for: (1) matching networkId to prevent cross-network attacks, (2) matching genesis hash ensuring same chain, (3) compatible forkId preventing incompatible protocol versions, (4) valid protocol version. Incompatible peers are disconnected immediately. The blockBitmask advertised by peers is considered untrusted and data availability claims must be verified through actual data retrieval attempts.

Blocks received from peers undergo comprehensive validation: (1) valid block header including parent hash chain, timestamp constraints, difficulty/consensus proof, (2) valid transactions with proper signatures and state transitions, (3) state root matches computed state after transaction execution, (4) gas limit and gas used within protocol bounds, (5) all fork-specific rules (Shanghai, Prague, etc.) are enforced. Invalid blocks are rejected and may result in peer disconnection.

Historical data requests are subject to: (1) rate limiting to prevent DoS, (2) resource bounds on result set sizes, (3) authentication/authorization checks where applicable, (4) validation of request parameters to prevent injection attacks. Responses are generated from validated local state or retrieved from peers with verification.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: EVM Execution Engine (CALL, DELEGATECALL, STATICCALL opcodes)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: External contract calls are protected by: (1) gas metering ensuring bounded execution, (2) STATICCALL enforcement preventing state modifications when used for read-only operations, (3) call depth limits preventing stack overflow attacks, (4) value transfer validation ensuring sufficient balance, (5) exception handling and proper revert semantics. The STATIC flag (EIP-214) ensures that read-only contexts cannot be violated by external code attempting state modifications (SSTORE, LOG, CREATE, SELFDESTRUCT, or value-transferring CALLs).

Historical data retrieved from peers via etha protocol is validated by: (1) verifying block hashes match known header hashes, (2) validating transaction receipts against receipt root in block header, (3) checking data integrity and completeness, (4) cross-referencing with multiple peers when available. Peers advertising data availability via blockBitmask may be dishonest, so failed retrieval attempts should trigger peer reputation penalties and alternative peer selection.

notes: All external entities identified across the 5 specification files have been classified and assigned boundary edges.
Two files (EIP-1052 EXTCODEHASH and Prague LOG opcodes) contained no external entities as they model purely internal EVM operations.
The EXT-PEER-NODE entity has two boundary edges (handshake and historical data retrieval) reflecting distinct security concerns.
The trust model emphasizes that all external inputs (transactions, blocks, peer data, RPC requests, external contract code) are untrusted and require comprehensive validation.
Special attention is given to the etha protocol (EIP-7801) which introduces new trust considerations around advertised data availability claims.
The STATICCALL mechanism (EIP-214) is recognized as a critical security primitive that creates a trust boundary preventing external contracts from violating read-only execution contexts.
